title: Children of the Heavenly King
description: Children of the Heavenly King in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Cennick wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 379 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Christian rejoicing in Hope”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Child-ren of the Heav-enly King, As ye jour-ney, sweet-ly sing; Sing your Sav-iour's wor-thy praise, Glo-rious in his works and ways.

lines: Glorious in his works and ways.
Ye are travelling home to God,
In the way the fathers trod;
They are happy now, and ye
Shout, ye little flock, and blest;
You on Jesus' throne shall rest;
There your seat is now prepared,
And we still will follow thee.

licence: Public domain: John Cennick died in 1755.
credits: Words by John Cennick (1718–1755), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. BEES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
